messages:
Maria Chen: Quick sync — engineering wants concrete launch criteria for structured-output (JSON mode + schema validation) so we can prioritize for Q2. Customer asks are coming in. Can we agree on V1 vs V2 behavior and rollback thresholds?

Chris Patel: TL;DR: Customers want two things: 1) an explicit JSON mode that reduces parsing work on their side, 2) server-side validation + optional auto-repair/retry. Many enterprise customers will only accept enforced schema for critical endpoints.

Devon Park: Implementation note: streaming + validation is the tricky bit. If we validate only at end-of-response we break streaming UX. Options: a) still stream tokens but buffer and run validation at end, b) enforce a final delimiter (e.g. `\n\n` + full JSON) and only mark success after validation. Both have perf implications.

Olivia Ruiz: Proposed launch split: V1 = "JSON-mode (best-effort)" + light validation warnings in headers. V2 = "Strict Schema" with automatic retry/repair and audit logging. V1 should be GA for hosted first, then Dedicated/Private.

Chris Patel: V1 asks we can commit to: - flag param `response_format=json` (best-effort) - header `x-json-parse` with status/warnings - docs showing how to do local fallback parsing. V2 must include explicit schema upload + per-request schema pointer.

Devon Park: For retries: we should limit to 1 auto-repair attempt server-side to avoid loops and cost blowups. Pseudocode: ```if validation_fails and attempts==0 and schema_is_strict: run_repair_prompt_then_rerun``` Repair should be logged with reason and token overhead estimate.

Maria Chen: Launch criteria proposal (vote): - Schema error rate <= 2% on canonical eval suite - Auto-repair success >= 60% when attempted - Additional p50 latency overhead due to validation < 100ms - No silent data loss; all repaired responses flagged in headers/logs - Rollback if error rate > 5% in production within 1h window

Olivia Ruiz: Also add telemetry: per-schema breakdown (errors, repairs, latency), per-customer opt-in strictness, and a canary rollout plan: 5% -> 25% -> 100% over 48h with manual gate at 25%.

Chris Patel: Priority note from sales: enterprise deals expect audit trail for strict mode and KMS integration for uploaded schemas. That bumps strict-schema earlier for big customers.

Devon Park: Edge cases: function/tool-calling + structured output. If model returns JSON that includes a function call object, we need to validate both the JSON envelope and the function payload shape. Might need separate schema namespaces.

Maria Chen: Decision draft: ship V1 (best-effort JSON mode + warning headers + docs) as low-risk Q2 item. Start V2 design now: schema registry + strict validation + one-shot repair flow + audit logging for Q3. Sales gets a private-beta for strict mode.

Olivia Ruiz: Metric thresholds agreed by team? If yes I'll add them to the RFC and the rollout checklist.

Chris Patel: +1 from me. Add go/no-go decision points: GA only after 2 weeks of canary with <2% error and no unresolved customer-red alerts.

Devon Park: I'll sketch the streaming validation options and a fail-open vs fail-closed matrix. Will post a short tech note by EOD.

release-bot: canary deployed to prod-5 at 1749004380 :rocket:

Maria Chen: Action items: Olivia -> update RFC with metrics & rollout. Devon -> tech note on streaming/repair. Chris -> gather top 3 enterprise schema asks. I'll schedule a follow-up sync next Tue. :thumbsup:
